primary_obstruction.name: EXTERNAL_SUBPALETTE_VS_SOURCE_LIST_SEMANTIC_MISMATCH
primary_obstruction.source_definition: For v outside S' union X0', CSZ defines L_{P'}(v) solely from colors on N(v) intersect S'.
primary_obstruction.external_mechanism: The P7-free List-3 algorithm reduces palettes by fixing singleton colors on possibly large sets and then updating neighboring palettes from those singleton vertices.
primary_obstruction.mismatch: If those singleton vertices are stored in X0', their colors constrain extensions but are invisible to L_{P'} of every other unseeded vertex.
primary_obstruction.axiom_v_effect: A vertex whose external palette has size <=2 but whose L_{P'} still has size 3 is required by axiom (v) to remain in source Y, not X.
primary_obstruction.lemma10_effect: Even if it is manually placed in X, Lemma 10 recomputes Z_i from |L_{P'}| and places it back in Y=Z_3.

direct_import_proof: Claims 14-16 of the external List-3 algorithm establish list-size reduction in the external palette, not in CSZ seed-list semantics.
CSZ explicitly states that L_P for an unprecolored vertex is determined by neighbors in S but not by neighbors in X0.
CSZ axiom (v) defines X/Y membership from the size of that seed-list.
CSZ Lemma 10 restores the canonical partition by setting Z_i={v:|L_{P'}(v)|=i}, then X=Z_2 and Y=Z_3.
Therefore storing the external algorithm's bulk singleton assignments only in X0' cannot, by itself, certify that the other externally reduced vertices leave source Y.
Moving a non-singleton 2-list vertex to X0' would require committing one color, which is an extra branching operation not supplied by the existing restriction theorem.
Moving enough palette-causing vertices into S' could reproduce some reductions, but the external theorem supplies no bound guaranteeing that a seed of size q(|S|) suffices.

schematic_witness.family: For any N, take S={a,b}, X0={x_1,...,x_N}, Y={y_1,...,y_N}, Y0={z_1,...,z_N}, X=empty; edges ab, a-y_j, x_j-y_j, y_j-z_j only; f(a)=1,f(b)=2,f(x_j)=3.
verified_properties: L_P(y_j)={2,3,4}, so every y_j is a source 3-list vertex in Y and has a neighbor in Y0.
Actual extension feasibility at y_j excludes color 3 because x_j in X0 is precolored 3, so the true palette relative to all fixed colors is {2,4}.
The source list remains {2,3,4} because x_j is in X0 rather than S.
schematic_witness.interpretation: This witnesses the semantic gap. It is not used to prove that every enhanced source-specific compilation is impossible.

retained_positive_value: The P7-free List-3 algorithm remains valid as an auxiliary structural/coloring tool.
Bulk singleton assignments can still be represented in X0' when only extension semantics, not source-list classification, is needed.
A future source-specific theorem could still exploit special B0/PATH_CELL geometry to convert a bounded subset of those restrictions into seed witnesses or safely remove affected components.
